Europe live with Jakub Krupa
Europe
Protests begin across France, with shops, businesses and tourist sites closed – Europe live
France will deploy 70,000 officers around the country, while protests are also expected in Italy, Spain, Austria, Portugal, Albania and Ireland
LIVE

1m ago
Frances Mao
Sat 24 Oct 2026 11.22 BST

From
1h ago
10.06 BST
Several of France’s leftwing political leaders have already shown up at the rallies in 
Orléans
 protesting against 
Marine Le Pen
 and her anti-immigrant party.
The demonstrations against “racism, fascism and imperialism” are being held as the National Rally’s congress takes place this weekend and Le Pen launches her presidential campaign.
“It was important for me to come here to Orléans,” said 
Bally Bagayoko, the mayor of Saint-Denis
, saying he was there to stand up against racism and the hate speech spread by the right.
He also directly referenced the “close link” between hateful rhetoric from parties like Le Pen’s, and the drive-by shooting outside of Paris on Friday morning which the town’s mayor had said appeared to be targeting people of African origin.
Sophie Binet, General Secretary of the CGT union
, also began her address to protesters by addressing the Trappes attack.
double quotation mark
I want to express our support and condolences to the victims, their families, and all the residents of Trappes.
This violence does not come from nowhere, it comes from speeches that convey racism, anti-Semitism, violence, which essentially come from the speeches of the far right
.
The 
Socialist party leader, Olivier Faure
, has also been seen in the crowds, marching behind an “All united against fascism” banner.

Opening summary
8m ago
11.15 BST
Paris protest route moved and pushed back to afternoon
Late last night, Paris police also ordered a change in the route for the main march that’s been organised by trade unions.
Originally, protesters had been given the green-light to march from Bastille to Nation squares in the centre, with the rally to commence in the late morning.
However, 
in their decree banning the route
, police said such a procession presented “
serious risks of public disorder, particularly due to the high density of businesses similar to those targeted during the 17-18 October weekend.”
Demonstrators can now only march from 
Porte de Vincennes and Porte d’Italie
 from 1pm to 7pm. Organisers scrambled together a legal appeal, which has failed, and 
groups are now preparing for a 2pm start.
 The new route is on the outskirts of the Parisian ring, through the 13th and 12th arrondisements.
Paris’s streets are pretty quiet at the moment. Police are out in full force guarding the main squares and government buildings, metro stations are closed, and most retail shops are closed or about to shut up shop.
View image in fullscreen
French riot police officers patrol Place de la Bastille this morning. The historic square, a symbol of the French Revolution, was the centre of protests last weekend
 Photograph: Mohammed Badra/EPA
Share
Updated at 
11.22 BST
32m ago
10.51 BST
Some protest bans overturned in last-minute court challenges
Following last weekend’s unrest, authorities across 
France
 moved to try to restrict demonstrations, limiting gathering numbers and march routes and issuing blanket bans in some cities.
That led to groups seeking permission for “authorised” protests with mixed results. For example, in Paris, the leading trade union was granted permission for their march while the Yellow Vest demonstrators were denied.
The bans have also sparked last-minute legal challenges from civil rights groups.
And now in the past hour, courts have overturned two protest bans – in the 
Bouches-du-Rhône prefecture and its capital Marseille 
and also in the city of 
Limoges
, which saw its centuries-old city hall set on fire last week.
Other cities that have bans in place for “unauthorised” demonstrations include:
Paris, Lille, Strasbourg, Mulhouse, Grenoble, Toulouse, Amiens
Of course, many protesters – from students to union groups – have said they will march anyway regardless of the bans or rules around where and when they can demonstrate.
Share
Updated at 
10.54 BST
1h ago
10.07 BST
Drive-by shooting outside of Paris targeted victims on skin colour
Angelique Chrisafis
The mood in Paris was heightened by fear and horror after what the government said was 
“racist, terrorist attack”
 in two towns west of the city on Friday.
A 26-year-old, well-respected martial arts star from a club outside Paris was killed and five other people were injured, including a 12-year-old girl shot eight times as a gunman pointed an automatic weapon from his car.
The French president, 
Emmanuel Macron
, said they were targeted because of the colour of their skin.
“These people were targeted because of their skin color or perceived religion, and for no other reason,” he said during his visit to Trappes, one of the affected towns, on Friday afternoon. “There is no place for this in 
France
.”
“There are no words,” wrote the sports club of the 26-year-old victim, the ATCH Academy. “Nothing could justify a life being torn away like this.”

Share
Updated at 
10.29 BST
1h ago
09.53 BST
Counter-demonstrators expected at Le Pen rally
Angelique Chrisafis
Tension was also high in the city of 
Orléans
 on Saturday as Marine Le Pen’s far-right, anti-immigration National Rally party gathers for its annual congress and the official launch of her presidential campaign.
The police presence in the city has been stepped up as around 5,000 party members and officials gather on Saturday and 10,000 attend Le Pen’s first campaign rally on Sunday.
A protest march by the left has been organised against “racism, fascism and imperialism”. Between 20,000 and 30,000 people are expected to demonstrate against the far right in the city.
Several political personalities on the left were to attend the Orléans march including the leader of the Socialist party, Olivier Faure, the head of the leftwing CGT union, Sophie Binet, and the mayor of Saint-Denis,
 Bally Bagayoko
, from the party La France Insoumise.
Share
Updated at 
10.06 BST
2h ago
09.38 BST
Paris closes 24 metro stations
The capital’s authorities have shut down the stations in a bid to contain crowds and curb movement throughout the city today.
 The affected stations are: 
Argentine, Assemblée Nationale, Bel Air, Champs-Elysées – Clemenceau, Charles de Gaulle – Étoile, Cluny - La Sorbonne, Concorde, Daumesnil, Dugommier, Franklin D. Roosevelt, George V, Mabillon, Maubert – Mutualité, Miromesnil, Odéon, Picpus, Rennes, Rue du Bac, Saint-Germain-des-Prés, Saint-Sulpice, Sèvres - Babylone, Solférino, Tuileries and Varenne.
We’ve seen other attempts by authorities to restrict movement in cities across 
France
 for this weekend; 
Marseille
 authorities earlier this week said they would suspend public transport services on Saturday; they were forced to reverse the decision following outcry.
In 
Orléans
, which is hosting the far-right National Rally congress, the tram lines are suspended and bike-sharing rentals have been removed from the city centre.
Share
Updated at 
09.39 BST
2h ago
09.15 BST
Angelique Chrisafis
View image in fullscreen
A jogger runs past a Societe Generale bank branch with its storefronts protected by wooden panels on the Champs-Elysees avenue in Paris ahead of nationwide protests on
October 24, 2026. 
 Photograph: Hannah McKay/Reuters
All through the night in neighbourhoods in the centre and east of Paris, the sound of sawing, drilling and hammering rang out as wooden boards were hastily secured into place to cover windows and shop-fronts.
Businesses being boarded up included opticians, supermarkets and pharmacies as well as trainers and handbag stores.
Hundreds of shops were smashed and looted over two nights last weekend in Paris, and thousands more in cities across 
France
, including Marseille and Bordeaux.
At a public meeting at Paris city hall this week, some shop-owners had cried as they spoke of their fears of businesses being smashed and looted again this weekend.
“I’m afraid there isn’t enough wooden board left to protect shops and the demand is making it so expensive to board up shops,” one optician near Châtelet in the city centre said. “We’ll close up and take all our stock of glasses out of the shop.”
View image in fullscreen
Workers install wooden panels to protect the windows of the gaming club Partouche Pasino Club in Paris 
 Photograph: Hannah McKay/Reuters
Share
2h ago
09.14 BST
Opening summary
Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of events in 
Europe
 – we will be closely following protests across the continent today.
In 
France
, hundreds of thousands are expected at rallies across the country, with high school students, unionists, “yellow vest” demonstrators and others turning out for a fourth weekend of protests demanding more government funding for schools and measures to help with housing and the cost of living.
Desperate to avoid the looting and property damage seen on the fringes of some protests last weekend, French authorities have ramped up restrictions on where protesters can march and which groups are “authorised” to do so. They’ve increased policing 20%, mobilising 70,000 police officers and soldiers to the streets, including both elite units and trainee officers.
Many of Paris’s metro stations and major museums and tourist sites are shut today, while across the country, shops and businesses have been urged to close their doors.
 Community tensions are also high following a deadly shooting on Friday west of Paris where the gunman targeted non-white people, killing one person and injuring five others including a child. The French president called it a “racist terrorist attack”.
Meanwhile, Marine Le Pen’s anti-immigration party is also due to hold its national conference in the central city of Orléans. The far-right National Rally’s meeting is expected to draw up to 30,000 counter-demonstrators.
 Protests are also being held in Italy, Spain, Austria, Portugal, 
Albania
 and Ireland today.
Stay with us for all the developments.
